Their pricing was competitive compared to other bids I received, and they offered a strong overall value for the work performed.

That said, I did run into a few bumps during the process. Coordinating with my home warranty company proved difficult — Ideal did provide diagnostic information, but follow-through on some requests and communication around those requests could have been smoother. On one of my early calls, the person who answered sounded a bit annoyed, and on subsequent calls I’ve occasionally felt like my call might be inconveniencing them. reviews_data.review_text:
UPDATE:
Shortly after posting my original review, 1st Choice Mechanical reached out immediately to ensure my complete satisfaction. While a quality control follow-up is standard practice and I had simply slipped through the cracks, they took full ownership of the situation without hesitation.

A representative came out, answered all of my questions, addressed my concerns, and got me scheduled to repair the scuttle. The response was professional, proactive, and reassuring.

From reception to sales to the technicians, every team member I interacted with was top-notch, friendly, professional, and genuinely committed to making things right. Their willingness to listen and act quickly speaks volumes about their customer service and integrity.

I truly appreciate how seriously they take feedback and customer satisfaction, and this follow-up experience reinforced my confidence in recommending 1st Choice Mechanical.

ORIGINAL:
After attending a home show, I learned that 1st Choice Mechanical was offering energy audits and decided to take advantage of the opportunity. The audit itself was very informative, and I discovered that both my ducting and AC system were not compliant for the size of my home. 1st Mechanical provided a detailed quote, and after obtaining three additional quotes that were roughly half the price, I circled back to them because I was genuinely impressed by their professionalism.

I asked why their pricing was significantly higher, and they took the time to reassess the project, lowered their price, and clearly explained the differences in scope and quality between their work and that of other HVAC companies. Based on that transparency, I ultimately chose to move forward with 1st Choice Mechanical and was scheduled for the same week.

The installation team arrived on time, were friendly, and worked efficiently. They completed the entire project in one day, which was impressive. However, I was disappointed with the housekeeping and communication surrounding the work. Insulation was left in clumps throughout my xeriscaping/landscaping, and there were no preventative measures taken to protect items in my garage. My washer, dryer, bikes, TV, and other belongings were covered in insulation dust, and no cleanup was done upon their departure. While it only took me about 30 minutes to clean everything with a leaf blower and towel, I would have prepared differently had I known what to expect.

Additionally, I was told the team would only be working in the attic over the house and not the garage, and I wasn’t advised to remove or protect any attic items. When I later inspected the attic, I found a white substance on a suitcase that I was unable to remove. The only direction I was given beforehand was to move my cars out of the garage. I also noticed insulation falling out of the vents throughout the house, requiring me to remove the vent covers and vacuum them myself.

They replaced the scuttle hole as part of the project, but the workmanship there was subpar. The staples were not fully secured, the wood was already cracked, and the cover is slightly too small for the opening. Lastly, there was no follow-up from the team to check on how the project went or to address any questions or concerns. While some of these issues may be standard practice, they were not communicated to me beforehand or discussed afterward.

Based on other reviews, I am confident the ductwork itself was done properly, and I appreciate the warranty, which gives me peace of mind as we head into summer. Overall, I would recommend 1st Choice Mechanical to friends and family for their professionalism, technical knowledge, and quality of work, but I do wish there had been better communication and attention to cleanup and customer follow-up.

August 16, 2025:

Justin came back out because the blower wasn’t turning on. After checking the furnace, he told us the blower motor was completely seized.
His exact words: the blower wheel “wasn’t put on right.”
And who was the last person to touch it? Dakota Anderson (#210).

It hasn’t even been a full year since Cool Zone last worked on that part. There is no reason I should be paying extra to fix damage caused by their own technician. Yet Cool Zone still tried to charge us full price for an issue they created.

reviews_data.review_text: Dan was awesome!   Very professional , and he shared valuable information that helped us make a good decision on which units to consider. His feedback was much appreciated. I look forward to working with Dan and AIRTIME!

I’ve reached the limit of my patience with Airtime. My experience has been a consistent pattern of missed diagnostics and negligent installation.

I bought my condo in August 2024. I have a ceiling-mounted 'pancake' unit (common in condos) that was only 3 years old but had a persistent grinding noise. Despite sending multiple technicians, Airtime was completely unable to diagnose the issue. One tech flat-out said, 'That's just what these units sound like' after only 10 minutes of looking. I assure you normal units do NOT make the grinding noise. Their inability to troubleshoot a relatively new system left me no choice but to buy a brand-new unit from them in March 2025.

The real issue arose nearly a year later. I had a routine service on Oct 20, 2025, and the tech failed to notice that a critical safety device (the float switch) was missing.

​My original installation invoice from March 2025 clearly lists—and charges me for—'"install new condensate overflow safety switch." Despite paying for this, it was never installed. For 11 months, I was unknowingly operating a system without the safety shut-off I explicitly paid for, leaving my home exposed to preventable flooding risks.

It wasn't until February 2026 that a Senior Technician (Garret) finally caught the error. He was shocked it was missing, telling me, "We install these on every single new unit. Every single one" To his credit, Garret was transparent and installed the part immediately, and informed his manager of the situation. However, fixing a safety hazard a year later does not excuse the fact that Airtime left my home unprotected for 11 months.

They couldn't fix my old unit, they failed to install critical safety parts on the new one, and their maintenance tech missed the error on October 20. Shout out to Garret for finally noticing, otherwise I'd still be unprotected.

​I cannot recommend a company that demonstrates this level of carelessness with safety equipment.

reviews_data.review_text:
TL;DR: Get a second opinion. Always. Don’t let them pressure you. We had two separate experiences with Bruce’s, and both felt more like pressure-based up-sells than actual service.

Most recently, they diagnosed our rooftop AC with two failing motors and quoted us over $2,000, pushing a “discount” if we signed up for their yearly subscription plan. The tech seemed okay, but the moment we said we wanted to think it over or compare quotes, we were suddenly put on the phone with a manager. That’s when the classic sales lines started:
• “We’ve been in business 50+ years”
• “No one else gives quotes over the phone” (Not true btw)
• “We’re not trying to sell you anything”
• “We’re just trying to help”
"We don't upsell"

It all felt scripted. And the way they got defensive so quickly just because we wanted a second opinion was a huge red flag. That’s what pushed us to get someone else immediately.

So we called another company (Semper Fi). Their tech inspected everything and found that the real issue was a refrigerant leak, which was what caused the motors to fail. Like Bruce’s, they also backed it up with photos, diagnostics, and a detailed breakdown.

I want to make it clear that Bruce’s findings were not wrong. But they only diagnosed the symptom, not the root cause. We would’ve spent thousands on a band-aid repair, with no fix to the underlying issue.

Earlier this year, we also had Bruce’s look at a portable AC problem. Instead of offering help, the tech spent over 20 minutes trying to pitch us on a “limited-time, exclusive” subscription plan and a NEW AC that we didn't need. He kept stepping outside to “talk to his boss,” then returned with more sales pressure (oh sorry, I meant he returned to "help" us). The manager got involved again (don’t remember if it was the same guy), repeating the “we’re just trying to help” line. Eventually, my mom had to outright tell them that we couldn’t afford it just to get them to stop and leave. In the end, we just paid someone on Thumbtack to fix the AC.

This company acts more like a sales team than a service provider. If you don’t believe me, test it yourself. Just say you want to think it over or something, and see how fast their tone will change.

reviews_data.review_text:
Spent 14k for two units from Hendels and had them come out every year to do the inspections.  After a fee years my compressor on one of our condensors starting making a lot of noise.  I was told that was normal and the women I spoke with even said hers does the same. If that were normal wouldn't it have done it from day one?  They said the only fix was a new compressor but it's under warranty right?  Technically yes but it still will cost $2200 to pay for freon!!! It doesn't need freon, they should be evac and recharging the freon.
For those that dont know AC systems are a closed system and should not need freon unless there is a leak. Mine does not have a leak. So essentially they want to charge me for my own freon. UNACCEPTABLE.

We also had a lot of problems during install with the the attic portion making noises in the house and they didn't believe us and although they eventually fixed it it wss unpleasant to say the least.

Judge a company of how they handle things when things go wrong not when everything goes right.

I had an issue with my condensation line and called Hendel’s around 3 PM. By 7 PM the same day, a technician was already at my home—no emergency fee, just great customer service. The tech had nothing but good things to say about the company and mentioned that his boss, Rob, was the best he’s ever worked for. I really appreciate a business that takes care of both its customers and its employees.

Called to check and see if they might have a Honeywell damper actuator for one I have that failed. Who ever answered the phone was like “damper actuator? We only sell generic parts” So I was like ok how about a generic damper actuator? “Hold on” and pretty quick came back and said “No we don’t sell those”.

I somehow find it hard to believe a place that has been around since 1970 would not have a damper motor / actuator. Bummer because this would’ve been a real quick sale, but I will have to find another dealer that would likely understand what I need. I can’t be the only person in the east Valley that has it zoned system.

This is what I was looking for Hendels.

Hi Chris Sabella,

We were surprised to see this review, especially given the timeline and the steps we took to resolve the issue in good faith.

Your system was installed on December 30, 2022, and the leak occurred on July 8, 2024 — more than 18 months after installation. When you contacted us, we responded promptly and found that the air handler had been shifted out of level, likely due to attic access by another party. Despite this being well outside the warranty period and not a result of our original work, we re-leveled the unit at no charge and offered to repair the ceiling — also at no charge, purely as a goodwill gesture.

The contractor we offered is an experienced professional we've trusted and worked with for several years, with no history of unhappy customers. When you declined that offer and went through your insurance instead, we fully respected that choice and cooperated with your insurer by sharing our findings.

We always strive to provide honest, quality service and to resolve concerns fairly — even when the cause appears unrelated to our work. We stand by how we handled this situation and regret that our efforts have been misrepresented here.

Roughly a month after our warranty expired, the associated AC unit failed. Wolfgang diagnosed the issue as a failed circuit board and recommended replacing the unit entirely with a Lennox system.

While seeking financing options, we obtained a second opinion from another company. To our surprise, they found that the AC unit itself was in excellent condition. Way over charged me for a capacitor replacement.   Knew I was in Colorado (snowbird), so charged me $1,264 to replace the capacitor.  Wasn't much I could do after he was already on site.  I now have an honest company on a service contract so that won't happen again.   The company I use now would have charged appox $200 (without the service contract) for the same work.  It was not an emergency trip that would have required extra charge. When I asked him why so much, he said you are paying for my expertise.  He was at the house for just over an hour.    Be careful.
Update - GCHS called me.   After talking to them I decided I really need to help others undestand that there are major issues with this company.   Core problem is the Invoice does not break out the work as parts, labor etc.  It is just one line item for $1264.  That is a MAJOR RED FLAG when a company does not break out their invoice (I've attached the invoice).  GCHS agrees they replaced the capacitor and connector and that they were there for appox one hour.  So let's see if we can recreate the invoice with details.  They installed a JARD 17425 connector (current price on Amazon is $33) and a MARS 14255 capacitor (current price on Amazon is $34).  We know companies increase the price of parts, so lets double it = $134.   Maybe just Roud to $200 to be on the safe side.   So $1264 (invoice) minus 200 for parts = $1064.  GCHS could not tell me where the $1064 went.  The only thing left is labor.  So they charged me $1064 for 1 hour of Labor.  GCHS could not explain this amount.  I was in Colorado and could not see the invoice until after I paid. I only used this company because my house watcher told me to contact them.   CAUTION - Don't use companies that don't itemize an invoice.  The current company I use is very honest.  I though most companies were, but apparently not.
I hope this saves someone else from a similar experience.
